questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses available, the culture of the country and what the University could offer me in terms of my career path

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was an amazing experience and I can highly recommend going on exchange!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Even though the experience was unforgettable, the application process was really difficult. The lack of information and late response rate was highly critical, so this is indeed negative aspects you have to deal with during the exchange-experience.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance from my host university, and other students. My experience was that my main students were actually the ones helping me the most, since the system is not working well for the student itself, unfortunately.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult,  but I found housing with two other students which indeed helped. Finding housing on your own can be very difficult, but I would also highly recommend living with other students while on exchange - so nice in a new city and a good way to meet other people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: From what I have heard, off campus worked often better than the on campus possibilities. But of course, you are more on your own and should be highly aware of the risks of scam.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I do not know myself.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very flexible. I could sign all the courses I wanted to, and there were no sudden restrictions. However, it is more difficult on your BA to find rights courses fitting your program. But my host university was not an obstacle in this matter,

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help from Professors and other students, also a mobility responsible person.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end successful, but it took some time to get courses approved by my Home University.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember that it is very common to figure out your courses while on exchange and not before. Do not stress about this, it is much more common than you think. And also, be prepared to change courses in last minute.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had courses on the MA-degree, even though I was at the BA, because I found the courses more interesting. This worked for me; I liked the higher level of the courses, and I would say the Italian academic level is different than the one in Copenhagen, but very funny to explore!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. Not as much reading as in Copenhagen, but on the other hand you were much more dependent on yourself and your own reading and knowledge.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Comparative Legal Traditions
Journalism, Media and Politics
Comparative Politics and Development
History of Regional Integrations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can highly recommend courses with the Professor Antonia Baraggia. She is excellent and also a coordinator of the Erasmus-students, and a lot of her courses are directed towards Erasmus-students. Professor Piero Graglia is also very friendly and his course (History of Regional Integrations) was fun to be a part of.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Books less expensive since a lot of them were online.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Too expensive for my budget, but heard it was nice.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot. Tennis, soccer, volleyball etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Day-trips out of the city and nights out.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips out of the city or hang around on your coffee house.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Italians are so warm and welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open and friendly. They are usually all very curious and friendly.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not much.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Italian coffee, the Italian vibe and the no strict deadlines at Uni. Of course you had deadlines, but they were not as time strict as in Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
There are plenty of courses and it can be difficult to navigate in the catalogue. 
Be aware of scam posts when you search for housing on your own
Have fun!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The personal and academic development.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adapting to a new academic culture and way of studying.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
